name: Thailand e-Visa
fullName: Thailand e-Visa: photo and passport page
covers: Bangkok, Phuket, Chiang Mai and the rest of Thailand
intro: Many travellers can visit Thailand without a visa for up to 30 days. If you need a visa, or plan to stay longer, you apply for a tourist e-Visa on the official site, thaievisa.go.th. The form asks for a recent photo on a white background and your passport's photo page, as JPG or PDF files of up to 3 MB each.

documents.label: Photo
notes: Taken within the last 6 months, on a plain white background.
A close-up of your face and the top of your shoulders; your face should fill 70–80% of the photo.
Uploads can be up to 3 MB. The site doesn't set a pixel size, so we make a sharp 35 × 45 mm passport-style photo, usually far smaller than the limit.

documents.label: Passport photo page
notes: The whole photo page, clear and readable, not cropped or blurred.
Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months from your travel date.
Screenshots are not accepted; photograph or scan the real page.

source.label: the Royal Thai Embassy, London (photo and upload rules)

facts.label: Do you need it?
facts.value: Many nationalities can visit visa-free for up to 30 days for tourism (the rules changed on 15 September 2026). If yours can't, or you'll stay longer, apply for the e-Visa.

facts.label: Cost
facts.value: Set by the Thai embassy for the country you apply from. For example, a single-entry tourist visa costs USD 40 from the US.

facts.label: Stay
facts.value: Up to 60 days on a tourist e-Visa, with one 30-day extension possible in Thailand.

facts.label: When to apply
facts.value: No earlier than 90 days before you travel, and ideally at least 30 days before.

steps: Go to thaievisa.go.th and create an account. Activate it from the verification email.
Start an application. The form checks your eligibility, then asks for your details, your photo and your passport photo page; upload the files you made here.
Add your travel details, then upload the supporting documents: flight booking, accommodation, recent bank statements and proof that you live in the country you're applying from.
Pay the fee online. It isn't refunded, even if the visa is refused.
Wait for the decision. The e-Visa arrives by email; print it and carry it with your passport.
beforeYouFly: Everyone, including visa-free visitors, must fill in the free Thailand Digital Arrival Card at tdac.immigration.go.th in the 3 days before arrival.
Each file you upload must be a JPG or PDF of 3 MB or less, and not password-protected.

faqs.q: What are the Thailand e-Visa photo requirements?
faqs.a: A photo taken within the last 6 months, on a plain white background, showing your face and the top of your shoulders, with your face filling 70–80% of the picture and no glasses. Files can be JPG or PDF up to 3 MB.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for Thailand?
faqs.a: Many nationalities can visit visa-free for up to 30 days for tourism. Check your nationality on thaievisa.go.th. You still need to fill in the free Thailand Digital Arrival Card before you land.

faqs.q: Can I apply for the Thai e-Visa from any country?
faqs.a: You apply through the Thai embassy for the country where you live, and the fee and documents follow that embassy's rules.
